skills.frame-analogize: Build and stress-test an analogy for a settled concept. Use for ELI5, metaphors, or 'explain differently'; compares candidates and names where the winner breaks.
skills.frame-draw: Decide how to picture something already understood: which form the question asks for, and which medium carries it (terminal, markdown, mermaid, interactive). Owns the strategy, not one format.
skills.frame-first-principles: Rebuild a question or decision from irreducible axioms, separating necessity from convention. Use to challenge assumptions or reason from first principles.
skills.frame-orthogonal: Factor a tangled problem into independent axes and verify that moving one leaves the others fixed. Use to expose conflated or falsely coupled dimensions.
skills.frame-tinker: Build a small interactive object to poke: one control, a visible before/after, details revealed on request. Rendering candidates to decide belongs to shape-mockup; choosing a picture belongs to frame-draw.
skills.frame-unfold: Walk someone through a repository, paper, book, or concept one layer at a time, skeleton first, choosing a form per layer. Use for progressive-disclosure walkthroughs; a single explanation or ELI5 belongs to frame-analogize.
skills.nav-audit: Audit codebase architecture against deep-module principles. Use for health, smells, feature-readiness, or full-domain reviews; read-only.
skills.nav-compose: Author or restructure prose: lead with the point, group by knowledge, and preserve claims and sources. Checking README/docs against implementation belongs to nav-sync.
skills.nav-do: Implement and verify authorized, already-decided fixes or multi-item tasks. Ground the approach in code; unresolved product choices and behavior-preserving refactors belong elsewhere.
skills.nav-plan: Ground an engineering approach in the code when asked for an implementation plan or to compare technical options. Use shape-task for delivery criteria and nav-do for decided builds.
skills.nav-refactor: Execute a behavior-preserving structural refactor with risk-proportional verification. Use to extract, split, or reorganize code without changing observable contracts.
skills.nav-ship: Land finished work: commit, push, merge into main (or open a PR when required), clean merged branches and worktrees, then run the project's documented tail. Making the change belongs to nav-do.
skills.nav-sync: Check or batch-update README and docs, or refresh code-file headers against current implementation. Verify claims and missing reader workflows. Project-record cleanup belongs to shape-tidy.
skills.shape-dogfood: Use a built feature through real browser or CLI workflows; evaluate tool friction and missing intents against the user's goal. Undecided comparative claims belong to shape-probe.
skills.shape-elicit: Clarify an undecided conceptual choice or specific root cause through grounded conversation. Ask only what changes the decision; explain small gaps inline. Not a visual comparison or permission to implement.
skills.shape-mockup: Converge a visual, structural, flow, or option decision through an interactive HTML artifact. Use to mock, compare, diagram, or try variants.
skills.shape-probe: Design a minimal experiment or assess existing measurements for an undecided claim. Judge what data supports; preferences and built-feature friction belong to shape-mockup / shape-dogfood.
skills.shape-idea: Capture or revisit a project idea, including something to consider later. Saving does not authorize implementation; clarifying a specific choice belongs to shape-elicit.
skills.shape-task: Record decided work with deliverables and acceptance checks. Use to queue work or start a feature that needs tracking. Idea capture belongs to shape-idea; a task-only request does not start implementation.
skills.shape-status: Recover current project work and next actions, or set priorities when explicitly requested. Reading status never authorizes implementation; graph views are disposable snapshots.
skills.shape-wrap: Save this round’s progress and next actions into the original project tasks before stopping. Explicitly invoked; no separate handoff or checkpoint.
skills.shape-tidy: Tidy stale project thoughts, completed plans, and redundant mockups with current reality while preserving useful decisions and reasons. README/code consistency belongs to nav-sync; explicit priorities to shape-status.
skills.shape-setup: Connect a code repository to its selected home workspace, reuse existing registration and verify the read path. Explicit setup only; environment scaffolding and legacy migration are separate.
